content.title: Rory McIlroy's Reason For Divorce And Reconciliation With Wife Erica Stoll Amid His 2026 Masters Win
content.text: Rory McIlroy has won the 2026 Masters Tournament, successfully defending his title to become only the fourth player in history to win back-to-back Green Jackets. With that, he equalled the record of Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, and Tiger Woods. Rory's stellar Masters victory, secured on April 12, 2026, marks his sixth major championship and his 30th career PGA Tour win. He finished with a 72-hole total of 12-under-par 276, one stroke ahead of world number one, Scottie Scheffler. As the 36-year-old Irish pro golfer leads the headlines, here's a look at his and his wife, Erica Stoll's divorce buzz. Why did Rory McIlroy file for a divorce against his wife, Erica Stoll? Rory McIlroy filed for a divorce against Erica Stoll in Florida on May 13, 2024, stating that their seven-year marriage was "irretrievably broken." Although no specific official reason for the split was released, reports hinted at several issues in their relationship. Insiders suggested that the couple was living "very different lives," as his constant travel for tournaments left her feeling "lonely". Erica reportedly had a hard time raising their little daughter, Poppy by herself while her husband was unavailable due to his job. Another unverified reason cited online was their different lifestyle choices. Rory is constantly in the public spotlight due to his career, while his wife prefers a quiet, private life, which reportedly added to the issues in their marriage. Amid the buzz around the divorce filing, unverified public speculation emerged about the golf star's link-up with sports reporter Amanda Balionis. Speculations surfaced suggesting a romantic connection between the two. Notably, the rumours were debunked, and both Rory McIlroy and Amanda maintained that their relationship was strictly professional. Even after the romance rumours and other issues, he and his wife, Erica Stoll have gotten back together. Rory McIlroy and Erica Stoll's reason for reconciliation Just after a month of divorce filing, Rory McIlroy filed a Notice of Voluntary Dismissal to end the divorce proceedings in June 2024. The official reason the couple shared with the media was a mutual realisation that they should prioritise their family, particularly their daughter, Poppy's well-being. During a conversation with The Guardian, he explained that the couple realised their "best future was as a family together." He later described the near-divorce situation in the Netflix series, Full Swing as a "wake-up call" that helped him realise how important his family and friends were. His statement to The Guardian was: "Over the past weeks, Erica and I have realised that our best future was as a family together. Thankfully, we have resolved our differences and look forward to a new beginning." Although Rory mentioned family being the prime reason for reconciling with Erica Stoll, the Daily Mail cited several other reasons. As per the report, the golfer was "unable to be on his own for more than five minutes." The second reason mentioned was that he wanted to avoid paying a huge chunk of his USD 26,80,64,000 fortune to lawyers as part of the divorce. His team reportedly supported his decision to withdraw the divorce filing, as they felt Rory had been too hasty in pushing for a split. Since their reconciliation, the couple has often been seen together at his match venues. Continue reading below More about Rory McIlroy and Erica Stoll Rory and Erica met in 2012 and became friends. They began dating in late 2014, shortly after he ended his engagement to Caroline Wozniacki. The golf star later told The Independent that he found it "refreshing" to be with someone who lived a "normal life" away from the spotlight. After about a year of dating, he proposed to her during a trip to Paris in December 2015. They got married on April 22, 2017, in a lavish ceremony at Ashford Castle in County Mayo, Ireland. After about three years of marriage, Rory and Erica welcomed their daughter, Poppy Kennedy McIlroy, in August 2020. What are your thoughts on Rory McIlroy and Erica Stoll's one-month separation?
